comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: Freshly retrieved 2026–2027 Applied Physics after-revision PER, Articles 3.3–3.5 and Appendix 2 pp.72–78, governs this ordinary English full-time programme. All 27 credited positions total 60 + 60 + 60 = 180: core 125 including exact 33BFP final project 15, ITEC 10 and genuine electives 45 (20 year two, 25 year three). No named specialization is required. All taught core units are 5 under the explicit quarter convention; 3SAFE is required noncredit safety training, not an extra 5-EC unit. PPD and first-/second-year challenges are embedded; MyFuture requires value seven without credits, and at least five Studium Generale activities belong within ITEC. Elective space requires examination-board approval and no substantive overlap, at least 30 credits at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3. The formal requirement list uses current Calculus 2MCALCAP, titled Calculus variant 3, replacing the earlier completed 2WCB0 option for pre-September-2026 students; the pilot appendix prints a different legacy code 2WBB0. These legacy references do not add another course or affect the current 5-credit position. The final project is a 15-credit block in Q4 or another quarter, or spread across two consecutive quarters. Entry requires 120 total, all compulsory first-year components, at least 110 core/ITEC credits and successful 33ACE; Appendix 2 permits meeting these conditions within 15 working days after starting, otherwise continuation stops. Laboratory components and project require successful 3SAFE. Future scheduling remains subject to applicable course conditions. No new UCR judgment is made.

alternatives.label: Mathematical systems, computation & intelligent technology
alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical models of dynamical systems through calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, programming, algorithms, image processing, machine learning, robotics and autonomous decision methods, with an energy-technology application strand. This is a computational related-fields response, not Applied Physics equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: Nineteen mathematical/computational courses and four energy/sustainability courses support the stated systems-and-technology direction; the label does not imply quantum, optical, electromagnetic or experimental-physics formation.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and nine advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes advanced algorithms and autonomous-system work; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and Renewable System Design.

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & sustainable technology
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical and computational models with Earth-system science, geospatial and laboratory investigation, water–mineral interactions, resource recovery, climate mitigation and renewable-system assessment to study natural physical systems and sustainable technologies.
alternatives.labelReason: Six Earth/environmental courses replace six specialist algorithmic courses, producing a substantive natural-system and resource-technology curriculum while keeping quantitative modelling central.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and eight advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource courses. Mathematical Methods precedes the later mathematics, robotics and neural-network courses. Environmental foundations precede the advanced biogeochemistry, recovery, resource and energy work.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. Optimisation, networks, algorithms, advanced algorithms, planning and reinforcement learning are replaced by Earth-system modelling, Dynamic Earth, soils/aquifers, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and advanced resource research. These changes implement a natural physical-systems direction rather than threshold-filling substitutions.

candidates.label: Natural physical systems and sustainable energy technologies
Optics, electromagnetism, devices and precision instrumentation

selection.assessment: Two coherent related-fields programmes pass the content, distinctness and feasibility gates. The first owns the mathematical, computational, dynamical and emerging-technology interests; the second adds a substantively different natural-system, laboratory, resource and energy direction. A quantum/nanoscale programme cannot supply quantum mechanics, atomic and condensed-matter physics or quantum measurement. An optics/electromagnetism/instrumentation programme cannot supply waves and optics, electromagnetism, circuits, sensors, precision measurement or experimental-device design. General modelling, image processing, sustainability science and environmental laboratories are not relabelled as those missing physics sequences.

notes.text: The UCR programmes develop mathematical and computational system models, autonomous technologies, natural-system analysis and sustainable energy/resource applications. They do not reproduce mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, quantum and condensed-matter physics, precision instrumentation, cumulative physics laboratories or the Applied Physics final project.
